transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I suppose occupational health sent me because of my eating habits at work. I’ve gotten into this pattern where I just... push breakfast and lunch aside, usually when I'm in the middle of long lab runs or exhibition work. And then, by the time I actually do sit down to eat, I keep it to something very small and controlled. So, they wanted me to come in and talk to you about it.
When you eat those small, controlled meals, do you ever make yourself vomit afterward, or use laxatives, or exercise excessively to compensate?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives. And as for exercise... no, I don't really work out excessively either. I just stick to the small amount of food I've planned out, and that's it.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past few months, and if so, are you concerned about your weight or how your body looks?

Yes, I have. My clothes are noticeably looser now, and... well, the numbers on the scale have just kept drifting down over the last few months. 

But as for being concerned about it... no, I wouldn't say I'm worried. Honestly, part of me actually sees the weight loss as a sign that I'm staying focused. There is so much unpredictability and chaos at work right now with the lab, and keeping my body like this... it just feels like I'm not letting all that chaos spill over into myself. It feels like I'm keeping things under control.
When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you look overweight or larger than you actually are?

Yes, I do. When I look in the mirror, like in the morning before I head to the lab, I really don’t see someone who is thin. I mostly just notice my stomach or my hips. And seeing those areas... well, it makes me feel as if they make me look careless, or just unserious.
Do you ever experience times when you eat a much larger amount of food than you normally would in a short period of time, where you feel like you've lost control during that eating episode?

No, I don't experience that. I don't really have times where I lose control over my eating. Like I said earlier, I stick strictly to the specific portions I've planned out for the day. Eating a large amount of food all at once... no, that just isn't something I do. I keep a very tight grip on what I consume.
